subject: Numeracy
title: Playing market
subtopics: Buying and selling up to five
objectives: Children will count out up to three or five items in a play market.
Children will use number, more and one each words in role play.
content: Using number, more, same and sharing words in a pretend market, counting out up to five items for customers.
teachingActivities: Take the role of a customer; ask for a number of items; model polite words; ask "How many?" and let children check.
learnerActivities: Set up a stall, count out items for customers, say please and thank you, and compare baskets.
resources: A table or cloth for the stall
A toy cash tin with large play coins
assessment: Check whether children count out the number asked for and use number words naturally in role play.
expectedOutcomes: Counts out items on request in play.
Uses number words naturally in role play.
crossCurricular: Understanding the world: markets and community helpers

lessons.title: Set up our market
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will help to set up a market and sort goods by kind.
successCriteria: Names goods and counts a few
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can count to five with support, share one each, add one more and use position and shape words.
lessons.starter: Say "We are opening a market today! Who will help me set up the stall? We need baskets for oranges, tomatoes and yams."
teacherActivities: Show a basket and name an item to place in it: "Oranges go in this basket."
Ask children to count how many items are in each basket, up to five.
Put a picture sign on each basket.
Walk around the market and say what you can buy.
learnerActivities: Children name the items and place them in baskets.
Children count items in their basket.
Children place a picture sign on the right basket.
Children say what they see.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show a basket and name an item to place in it: "Oranges go in this basket." Children: Children name the items and place them in baskets.
Step 2. Teacher: Ask children to count how many items are in each basket, up to five. Children: Children count items in their basket.
Step 3. Teacher: Put a picture sign on each basket. Children: Children place a picture sign on the right basket.
Step 4. Teacher: Walk around the market and say what you can buy. Children: Children say what they see.

practical.title: Market set-up
steps: Give each pair a basket and a set of toy items.
Sort the items and count them.
practical.safety: Use toy items only; keep the stall low and stable; children walk calmly.

differentiation.support: Sort two kinds of item and count only three.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to label the basket with a picture and tell a friend how many.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Stand back and admire the market. Say "Our market is ready!"
lessons.homeConnection: Talk about what you buy at the market and how many.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "help to set up a market and sort goods by kind" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Buying and selling
lessons.subject: Numeracy
lessons.subtopic: Buying and selling up to five
objectives: Children will buy and sell up to three items, saying please and thank you.
successCriteria: Counts out the number of items requested
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can count to five with support, share one each, add one more and use position and shape words.
lessons.starter: Act as a customer. Say "Good morning. Please may I have two oranges?" Wait for the trader to count out two oranges.
teacherActivities: Model the buying and selling exchange with a child as the trader.
Ask for three tomatoes and let the trader check by counting.
Let pairs take turns as customer and trader with number cards.
Swap roles and try a number up to five.
learnerActivities: Child counts out two oranges and says "thank you".
Child counts three tomatoes and gives them.
Pairs buy and sell and count aloud.
Children count out up to five items.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Model the buying and selling exchange with a child as the trader. Children: Child counts out two oranges and says "thank you".
Step 2. Teacher: Ask for three tomatoes and let the trader check by counting. Children: Child counts three tomatoes and gives them.
Step 3. Teacher: Let pairs take turns as customer and trader with number cards. Children: Pairs buy and sell and count aloud.
Step 4. Teacher: Swap roles and try a number up to five. Children: Children count out up to five items.

practical.title: Market role play
steps: Set up a stall for each pair.
The customer shows a number card.
The trader counts out that many items.
practical.safety: Use toy items only; keep stalls stable; supervise role play.

differentiation.support: Use number cards 1 and 2 only and count together.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to buy two different things and say how many in all.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: How many tomatoes did you buy?
What do we say when we receive something?

lessons.conclusion: Close the market stall and say "Goodbye, see you tomorrow."
lessons.homeConnection: Pretend to shop at home using real items and ask for numbers.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "buy and sell up to three items, saying please and thank you" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Which basket has more?
lessons.subject: Numeracy
lessons.subtopic: Buying and selling up to five
objectives: Children will compare baskets from the market and say which has more or the same.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can count to five with support, share one each, add one more and use position and shape words.
lessons.starter: Show two baskets of fruits and say "Who has more fruits? Amina or Tunde? Let us count."
teacherActivities: Count the fruits in each basket by moving one at a time.
Say "Amina has four. Tunde has three. Amina has more."
Make the baskets the same by giving one more to Tunde.
Let pairs make baskets and compare them.
learnerActivities: Children count each basket aloud.
Children say "more" and point to Amina’s basket.
Children add a fruit and say "same".
Pairs compare and say more or same.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Count the fruits in each basket by moving one at a time. Children: Children count each basket aloud.
Step 2. Teacher: Say "Amina has four. Tunde has three. Amina has more." Children: Children say "more" and point to Amina’s basket.
Step 3. Teacher: Make the baskets the same by giving one more to Tunde. Children: Children add a fruit and say "same".
Step 4. Teacher: Let pairs make baskets and compare them. Children: Pairs compare and say more or same.

practical.title: Compare baskets
practical.safety: Use toy fruits only; keep baskets on the mat; supervise group play.

differentiation.support: Compare baskets of one and four items.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to say how many more one basket has.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: Are they the same?
questions.expected: Yes or no with a reason.

lessons.conclusion: Count both baskets and say "More, same."
lessons.homeConnection: Compare two plates of food at home and say which has more.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "compare baskets from the market and say which has more or the same" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

pictures: Two baskets with different numbers of fruits

lessons.title: Sharing market goods
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will share market goods fairly among friends and count them.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can count to five with support, share one each, add one more and use position and shape words.
lessons.starter: Say "After the market, the family shares the fruits. One for you, one for you, one for you. How many do we have left?"
teacherActivities: Give out one fruit to each plate and count how many are left in the basket.
Ask "Is there enough for everyone?" Add more if needed.
Share fruit among three plates and say "one each, one each".
Count the fruits on each plate and say they are the same.
learnerActivities: Children count the fruits left.
Children check and add fruits.
Child shares one fruit to each plate.
Children count and say "same".
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Give out one fruit to each plate and count how many are left in the basket. Children: Children count the fruits left.
Step 2. Teacher: Ask "Is there enough for everyone?" Add more if needed. Children: Children check and add fruits.
Step 3. Teacher: Share fruit among three plates and say "one each, one each". Children: Child shares one fruit to each plate.
Step 4. Teacher: Count the fruits on each plate and say they are the same. Children: Children count and say "same".

practical.title: Share the shopping
steps: Give each group a basket and plates.
practical.safety: Use toy fruits; keep baskets on the table; supervise group play.

differentiation.extension: Ask the child to share five fruits among two plates and say what is left.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: Does each plate have the same?

lessons.conclusion: Pack the baskets away and say "Thank you, market."
lessons.homeConnection: Help share fruit or biscuits fairly at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "share market goods fairly among friends and count them" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Market stations
lessons.subject: Numeracy
lessons.subtopic: Buying and selling up to five
objectives: Children will show they can count, compare and share in a market game at three stations.
successCriteria: Counts out up to three or five items
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can count to five with support, share one each, add one more and use position and shape words.
lessons.starter: Sing the market song and show the three stations.
teacherActivities: Rotate groups every four minutes and observe one station closely.
Ask "How many would you like?" and "Which has more?"
Record each child’s level and take photographs.
learnerActivities: Children play at each station.
Child counts and answers.
Children tidy at the signal.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Rotate groups every four minutes and observe one station closely. Children: Children play at each station.
Step 2. Teacher: Ask "How many would you like?" and "Which has more?" Children: Child counts and answers.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level and take photographs. Children: Children tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Station circuit
practical.safety: Use toy items only; supervise stations; keep floors clear.

differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to be the market manager and help a friend.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: counts out items on request; uses number, more and same words in role play; shares one each.

questions.question: Can you give me three oranges?

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 9
Uses number words in role play
lessons.conclusion: Sing the market song and tidy up together.
lessons.homeConnection: Play market with real objects at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "show they can count, compare and share in a market game at three stations" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?
